mainEntity.name: How Does Zero-Pressure Accumulation Work on a Case Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zero-pressure accumulation divides the conveyor into zones controlled by sensors. When a downstream machine pauses, each case stops in its own zone instead of pushing against the case ahead, so cases are not compressed and restart in order. In accumulating conveyor systems built with TRFIntraflow, it is a standard flow management module, sized for the stops your line has to absorb.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Merge, a Divert and a Sorting Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A merge combines cases from two or more conveyors onto one path. A divert sends cases from the main path to another lane, such as a second palletizer or a reject lane. A sorting system uses product data, such as a barcode, to send each case to its assigned destination. TRFIntraflow includes merge, divert, sorting and reject station modules under one control system.

mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Integrate With My Palletizer and Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFIntraflow includes palletizer interfaces, machine communication, sensors, PLC and HMI as standard integration modules. TRF connects the conveyors to case packers such as TRFOnepack and TRFDroppack, to palletizers such as TRFCobot and TRFCompact, and to equipment already installed in your plant. Each interface is defined during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: Can a Single Supplier Engineer, Build and Install My Entire Conveyor System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRF takes ownership of TRFIntraflow projects from concept and engineering to manufacturing, controls, assembly, installation and commissioning, within one coordinated delivery model. One partner answers for the complete intralogistics solution, which reduces the integration risk of combining sections, controls and interfaces from several suppliers. The same team can also integrate the case packers and palletizers at both ends.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Custom Conveyor System Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the number of lines served, line rates, case size and weight, the layout and floor space, the number of accumulation, routing and elevation points, and the interfaces with case packers, palletizers and warehouse systems. TRFIntraflow is always quoted as a complete engineered system.

mainEntity.name: Can Roller, Belt and Modular Belt Conveyors Be Combined in One System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFIntraflow combines powered roller, belt and modular belt conveying with transfers, curves, turntables, accumulation, merges, diverts and elevation modules in one coordinated system. TRF selects each module for the unit conveyed, the path it follows and the function of that segment, then connects it with sensors, PLC, HMI and machine communication, so the whole line runs under one control logic.
